about: Every place-specific figure the town generator uses for a small town in interior Minas Gerais, Brazil, with its source. The reference municipality is Aguanil, MG (IBGE code 3100807; 4,357 residents in the 2022 Census; Campo das Vertentes / south-central Minas): its Census 2022 age structure, households, tenure and religion, and its 2024 municipal accounts, are used directly; state (Minas Gerais) figures are used where no municipal figure exists, and national ones where no state figure exists. Fortnightly wages and payments are the monthly Brazilian figures converted (x 12 / 26) because the structure pays on 14 days. Values still marked placeholder say what they were estimated from. A world for another place and time is another profile; the platform's code holds none of these (docs/profiles.md). SINCE 2026-10-09 (employment.*): the profile states the share of employees' jobs that are registered and the share and kinds of own-account work; the town holds the own-account traders (about 5% of people in work), and the other kinds are still drawn as employees.

sources.culture.conducts: What people start out holding right, for the four conducts where a figure in this profile's own outlook speaks to it (the rest start from values alone: no figure was opened). approves_bps is the national share with 'a great deal' or 'quite a lot' of confidence, as `outlook.trust` has it (World Values Survey and European Values Study, joint wave 7, as Our World in Data publishes it; opened 2026-10-11, to confirm against the survey's tables; see sources.outlook for the country and the items). Mapping, ours: answer_tribunal and take_to_tribunal <- confidence in the courts (a person who trusts the courts approves of answering a case there and of taking a wrong to it); complain <- confidence in the civil service (writing to the town is approved where the town's officers are trusted to answer); join_union <- confidence in labour unions. Weak: confidence in an institution is not approval of an act toward it, and the share above a threshold is read as a mean, as outlook does; the figure sets where people start (their own lean and their picture of what others approve), nothing else, and the lean is measured from it, so the rates stay the calibrated ones. No figure for strike, take_in, stay_past_notice, take_from_employer or an organisation's conduct (the survey's items on joining strikes and on the justifiability of stealing property were not opened); no figure by origin group (no source found that gives one). National, not the place's. does_bps is never given: a conduct's own rate in the profile. 2026-10-16: the national confidence shares it takes from the survey were opened as data (see outlook).
sources.culture.origin: PLACE: Aguanil (municipality 3100807), Censo 2022, cor ou raca (the census's own classes, self-declared). groups: IBGE, Censo Demografico 2022, SIDRA table 9605, percent of residents, Aguanil: branca 57.33%, parda 34.96%, preta 7.55%, amarela 0.05%, indigena 0.11% (https://apisidra.ibge.gov.br/values/t/9605/n6/3100807/v/1000093/p/2022/c86/2776,2777,2778,2779,2780, opened 2026-10-16); the town's own shares replace the state's (Minas Gerais: branca 41.08%, parda 46.76%, preta 11.84%, amarela 0.15%, indigena 0.16%, the figures this profile held until 2026-10-16: the town's white share is 16 points higher and its parda share 12 lower). same_household_bps: 6930 = 69.3% of Brazilian couples of the same cor ou raca, IBGE Censo 2010 (white 74.5%, pardo 68.5%, indigenous 65.0%), as reported by Zero Hora 2012-10-18 and reproduced at https://ihu.unisinos.br/514657-censo-retrata-um-novo-perfil-da-familia-brasileira , OPENED 2026-10-13 (the IBGE table itself not opened). National, 2010, not Aguanil 2022. homophily_bps: PLACEHOLDER 5000 (a close tie is half again as likely within a group as by chance). No survey of close ties or friendship by group for this place was found and opened; McPherson, Smith-Lovin and Cook 2001 ('Birds of a feather', Annual Review of Sociology 27) gives the general fact, not this place's figure. CHILDREN: cor ou raca is declared by the household for each member, and 'parda' takes in many of mixed descent, so a child of a mixed couple is often declared parda, not either parent's group: the generator's rule does not fit well (to confirm; the census says nothing on this in the pages opened).
sources.tenancy.rent_share_of_income: IBGE, Sintese de Indicadores Sociais 2024, Tabela 3.23 (onus excessivo com aluguel), Brazil 2023: in 26.99% of rented households the monthly rent was 30% or more of household income (25.95% in 2022) (https://ftp.ibge.gov.br/Indicadores_Sociais/Sintese_de_Indicadores_Sociais/Sintese_de_Indicadores_Sociais_2024/Tabelas/xls/3_Moradia_xls.zip, opened 2026-10-12). National: for Minas Gerais only the share of people is published (19.83%, Tabela 3.22). IBGE publishes that one threshold and no other band, median or mean, so there are two bands: under 30%, and 30% or more. Gross household income from all sources; rent alone; households without income are left out by the source. HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/generator.md, "Homes by income"): each renting household of a new town draws its share from these bands (evenly within a band; the open band from its lower bound to twice it, at most everything), which gives the rent it carries; households and let homes are matched by it. A target as well: the town's own distribution at the start is reported beside it and is not fitted to it.

HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/generator.md, "Payments in force"): of those the payment's rule already entitles as the year begins, this share open with it in payment; the rest claim it when they first look, as before.
sources.ownership.owner_bps_by_age: A PROXY: IBGE publishes no tenure by age of the household's reference person in the tables found. Residents of occupied private dwellings by their own age, Minas Gerais, Censo 2022 (IBGE, SIDRA table 9938, https://servicodados.ibge.gov.br/api/v3/agregados/9938, opened 2026-10-12): living in a home a resident owns: 64.4% at 15-34, 70.6% at 35-44, 77.2% at 45-54, 82.6% at 55-64, 86.5% at 65 and over. People, not households: used for the slope by age only. HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/generator.md, "Homes by income"): only as how much likelier a household of one age is than another to be among the town's owners; their number is the houses the profile's house_owner_bps makes owner-occupied.
sources.households.kin_households_most_bps: 13.90%: extended domestic units (unidade domestica estendida), Minas Gerais (IBGE, Censo Demografico 2022, SIDRA table 9879, https://servicodados.ibge.gov.br/api/v3/agregados/9879/periodos/2022/variaveis/800?localidades=N3[31]&classificacao=460[all], opened 2026-10-12; IBGE's own definition of the category was read only in a search summary: to confirm). sources.tenancy.possession: Lei 8.245/1991 (Lei do Inquilinato), arts. 9, 59 and 62 to 63: an action for eviction for unpaid rent; the tenant may cure by paying within 15 days of being served; an order gives 15 days to vacate (to confirm: recalled, the law not opened). arrears_days 30, notice_days 30 and warrant_days 15 are PLACEHOLDERS; plan_months 0 (the cure is payment in full). The police stand for the court's officer. The two shares of how tenants answer are the same in every profile: stay_past_notice_bps 5000 is a PLACEHOLDER (no figure was found for the share of tenants who stay past a notice for arrears); leave_on_order_bps 5900 is England's, used everywhere: of 16,848 landlord possession orders in January to March 2026, 6,888 repossessions were by county court bailiffs, 41%, so about 59% of those ordered out were gone without one (Ministry of Justice, Mortgage and Landlord Possession Statistics, January to March 2026: opened by a research agent for this work, 2026-10-11; a ratio of one quarter's flows, not of one cohort). eviction_notice_days: the notice of the day that whoever carries out a warrant gives the tenant; England's county court bailiffs give 14 days' notice of an eviction (Civil Procedure Rules 83.8A: to confirm, recalled), Germany's Gerichtsvollzieher about three weeks (to confirm); every other place's figure is a PLACEHOLDER (7 days; Ohio 3, within its ten). HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/justice.md, "Possession"): published in the town as a law; a landlord gives a notice to vacate under it, applies to the tribunal if the tenant stays, and asks for a warrant if they stay past its order; the tribunal sets a plan or a date by it; the police carry the warrant out. Tenants who answer, and plans (2026-10-12): answer_bps 4000 is a PLACEHOLDER (no figure was found for this place of how many tenants served with an application for possession answer it in writing or attend; it is the middle of the two figures opened for other places: 43% of hearings with the renter or someone for them in Victoria, 39.3% of tenants present in Cleveland, Ohio). plan_consider 'none' and cure_days 15: the court sets no plan; the tenant may end the claim by paying everything owed into court within 15 days of being served (Lei 8.245/1991 art 62, purgacao da mora: recalled, to confirm, the page could not be opened). 2026-10-16: the statute is now opened (planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/leis/l8245.htm): the tenant is cited and has 15 days from service to pay and avoid termination (art 62 II, as amended by Lei 12.112/2009; the tenant or the guarantor may pay): cure_days 15 agrees; an eviction order gives 30 days to vacate, but 15 where the eviction is ordered under art 9 (non-payment is art 9 III) or more than four months passed between service and the first-instance sentence (art 63 and its para 1): possession_days 15 agrees for arrears. A liminar (an interim order, in 15 days, against a deposit of three months' rent, art 59 para 1) is not modelled (the list of cases was not read in full). arrears_days 30, notice_days 30 and warrant_days 15 stay placeholders.
sources.business.entry_bps_per_year: IBGE, Demografia das Empresas e Estatisticas de Empreendedorismo 2021 (Estudos e Pesquisas, Informacao Economica n. 37, published 2023, https://biblioteca.ibge.gov.br/visualizacao/livros/liv102036.pdf, text extracted and opened 2026-10-16): entry rate of enterprises 17.8% in 2021 (21.8% in 2008), of local units 17.5% (exit 11.5%). 1780 is the enterprise rate. National, formal enterprises with a CNPJ in CEMPRE (not own-account informal work), 2021; Minas Gerais's own rate was not recoverable from the table. Replaces the PLACEHOLDER 1700 (recalled, 15 to 20%). HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/entry.md, "Starting a business of one"): the generator turns it into a monthly chance for those who could start a business of one (in the labour force, of working age, with the savings for its stock), from the businesses the town has: births a year at this rate, over those people. Most real births are businesses with no employees, which is the only kind that can be started here without premises.
sources.employment.hours: Constitution art. 7 VI (pay irreducible except by collective agreement or convention) and XIII (44 hours a week); CLT art. 503 (a general reduction of pay for proven losses, by no more than 25%, never below the minimum wage); Lei 4.923/1965 art. 2 (a reduction of hours with proportional pay of up to 25%, by agreement with the workers' union, for up to three months, renewable) (to confirm: none opened; read from search results 2026-10-13, which say art. 503 and the Law are partly superseded by the Constitution). Simplified here: the union's agreement stands as the worker's agreement (consent), at least 75% of the ordinary hours, 90 days a spell, pay in proportion (nothing owed beyond it). The 2020 wage-support scheme (Lei 14.020) was temporary and is not modelled. HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/firms.md, "Hours before heads"): published in the town as a law (law-cutting-hours); a shop or factory over its need cuts everyone's hours to what its trade needs before it lets anyone go, where this says it may, and pays what it owes for the hours cut; a worker reads the employer's paper as the pay agreed. consent_bps 9000 is a PLACEHOLDER (of workers asked to agree to a cut as the alternative to someone being let go, the share who do; no figure found). The employer's own notice of 3 days is ours, so that the paper reaches the worker first.
sources.employment.adjustment: PLACEHOLDERS, the same in every profile, with a sourced shape (docs/behaviour/firms.md, "Adjusting labour"; docs/research/references.md). smooth_months 3: firms plan production and workforce on smoothed, forecast trade and not on the last period's (Holt, Modigliani, Muth and Simon 1960); no figure for the horizon of a small employer here was found. hiring_cost_weeks 8: what recruiting and training a new worker costs, in weeks of their pay; estimates run from under two weeks to over sixteen (Silva and Toledo 2009; Manning 2011; Blatter, Muehlemann and Schenker 2012; Muehlemann and Leiser 2018: all to confirm, none opened), and none is for this place.
sources.employment.termination: Constitution art. 7 XXI and Lei 12.506/2011 (aviso previo: 30 days and three more for each year of service, to 90); Lei 8.036/1990 art. 18 (a fine of 40% of the FGTS balance on dismissal without cause; the balance builds at 8% of pay, so the fine is about 1.66 weeks' pay for each year of service: derived) (to confirm: recalled by a research agent for this work, 2026-10-11, the statute not opened). HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/firms.md, "Adjusting labour"): published in the town as a law; an employer reads it before letting someone go for redundancy (what it would owe is part of what the job costs to end) and pays what it says when the job ends. Service is counted from the start of a run: nobody's earlier years with an employer are known to it.
sources.frictions: Everyday frictions (docs/behaviour/frictions.md): what goes wrong, how often, and how the bodies that hear it work. Read by the generator only for a town whose spec has `living`.
sources.frictions.per_adult_bps_per_year: Of adults, the share who had each kind of problem, a year: half the share who had it in the last two years in World Justice Project, Global Insights on Access to Justice 2019 (General Population Poll 2017-18, about 1,000 respondents a country; the summary statistics workbook was opened; national, and for Brazil and Mexico the three largest cities only). landlord: a problem with a landlord over agreements, payments, repairs, deposits or eviction (4.5% in two years; all of it is given to disrepair here, which overstates repairs: the town has no other landlord problem of the kind yet). wages: difficulty obtaining wages or employment benefits agreed in advance (4.2%). bill: major disruption of a utility's supply or incorrect billing (17.9%; all of it is given to wrong bills). benefits: difficulty obtaining public benefits or government assistance (2.4%). goods: a consumer problem (32.0%) less the utility share, since the survey's consumer problems include it (derived; poor professional services are in it too). The generator turns each into a rate for those exposed (a let dwelling, a job, a customer, a claim) with the town's own counts. Halving a two-year share understates a yearly one where people have a problem in both years (to confirm against a yearly survey). 2026-10-16: no better source found for bill, wages, put_right_on_asking, pay_short_by_bps, bill_over_bps, goods_faulty_share_bps, repair_hours (Aneel, Procon, Senacon, PNAD, DIEESE searched: complaint totals only).
sources.frictions.put_right_on_asking_bps: Asked to put it right, how often the other side does. PLACEHOLDERS, every one: each stands at the share of people with any problem who say it is done and fully resolved (54.7%: World Justice Project, Global Insights on Access to Justice 2019 (General Population Poll 2017-18, about 1,000 respondents a country; the summary statistics workbook was opened; national, and for Brazil and Mexico the three largest cities only)), which is an outcome of everything people tried, not the rate at which the other side agrees when asked: to replace with a figure by kind of problem.

sources.frictions.support: (Until foundations F6 this note also gave a processing time, a placeholder fortnight, and a daily capacity; both are gone: how long a claim takes is the hours of whoever decides it.) wrong_refusal_bps: of claims that qualify, the share wrongly refused. FITTED in the 1,000-person town of the first profile (7% of qualifying claims gives about as many refusals a year as 6% of adults, its survey share with difficulty obtaining public benefits, counting the refusals that are right), and for every other place scaled by its own survey share against that one: a stand-in until a place's own rate of decisions changed on review is found. 2026-10-12: this fit assumed every entitled person claims in the year. A town now opens with the payments its people are already entitled to in force (granted before the year, never decided in it), so it decides fewer claims and refuses fewer (Victoria 37.8 to 24.8 a year). It is NOT re-fitted: that would be fitting an outcome again. Reviews of payments in force, which would add wrong stops, were looked for in this place's law and statistics and no rate of wrong stops per review was found; nothing is built (docs/behaviour/frictions.md, 'Payments in force are not reviewed'; docs/decisions.md, 2026-10-12, 'Reviews of payments in force'). 2026-10-16 (not applied): the Tribunal de Contas da Uniao's audit of INSS decisions, as reported in the press (https://previdenciarista.com/blog/inss-erra-em-mais-de-10-dos-pedidos-negados/, opened; the audit itself, its acordao number, not found), found 13.2% of manually analysed denials in 2023 wrongly denied (10.94% of automatically processed ones, January to May 2024), about 250 to 290 thousand of 14.4 to 16.8 million applications, 1.7 to 1.8% of all applications: the same order as 140 if read per application, about eight times it if read as a share of denials; the denominator decides, federal and national, so 140 stays the fitted stand-in. The appeals council's reversal of about 20% (2023; a snippet) was not located on an opened page.

sources.outlook: How people start out in what they trust (docs/behaviour/citizen.md, 'The record'). National figures for Brazil, not the region's: none by region was found. trust: the share with 'a great deal' or 'quite a lot' of confidence in each kind of institution (`government`, `policing`: the police, `courts`, the civil service, banks, the press, labour unions, churches or religious organisations, major companies); people_bps: the share who say most people can be trusted. World Values Survey and European Values Study, joint wave 7 (fieldwork 2017 to 2022), as Our World in Data publishes it (ourworldindata.org/grapher/trust-state-institutions-wvs, trust-organizations-wvs, self-reported-trust-attitudes), opened 2026-10-11 through a tool that returns a page's figures in summary: to confirm against the survey's own tables. The share is read as the mean level of trust a person starts with, which is a simplification (a share above a threshold is not a mean). Not stated, so the citizen's own placeholders apply (to source: the survey's question on freedom of choice and control over one's life, its mean and spread, needs the microdata): how much control over their lives people feel (outlook.agency). 2026-10-16: every figure above read again from the full Our World in Data CSVs (https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/trust-state-institutions-wvs.csv, trust-organizations-wvs.csv, self-reported-trust-attitudes.csv, Brazil, year 2022) and found to agree to the digit: courts 50.32, police 54.15, civil services 48.79, government 22.56, press 37.23, labour unions 32.49, churches 66.91, banks 49.99, major companies 52.31, trust in others 6.52. Opened as data now, not in summary; OWID republishes the survey, whose own tables were not compared.
sources.outlook.residence: PLACEHOLDER: no figure for how long people have lived at their address was found for Brazil on a page opened. Borrowed from Australia's (the only place whose figures were opened), for lack of any: ABS, 2021 Census, 'Population movement in Australia' (released 8 November 2022; abs.gov.au/articles/population-movement-australia), opened 2026-10-11: 53.1% of the population lived at the same address five years before the Census; 14.3% changed address within Australia in the year before; 0.7% had lived overseas a year before. Bands here: under 1 year = 14.3 + 0.7 = 15.0%; 1 to under 5 = the rest (31.9%); 5 and over = 53.1%. They are built from the one-year and five-year mobility rates, so the 1 to under 5 band is the remainder, and the 5-and-over share is the share at the same address five years earlier (population aged 5 and over, not adults only). National figures, not Victoria's: the Victoria figures were not found on an opened page. The open band is read as 5 to 15 years by the generator. Brazil's own are probably different (to source: Census or housing-survey tables of years since moving in).
sources.outlook.job_tenure: How long employed people have been with their current employer (starting attachment to the trade). OECD, 'Employment by job tenure intervals' (dataset OECD.ELS.SAE DSD_TENURE@DF_TENURE_FREQ, measure TENURE_EMP, share of employment by time with the current employer; both sexes, all ages), national figures for Brazil, 2024; read from the OECD SDMX API (sdmx.oecd.org/public/rest/data/OECD.ELS.SAE,DSD_TENURE@DF_TENURE_FREQ) on 2026-10-11, the response opened and the figures copied: under 1 year, 1 to under 3, 3 to under 5, 5 to under 10, 10 and over. National, not the region's: none by region was found. It covers the employed (employees and the self-employed), where a person's tenure is the time in the present job. The open band (10 and over) is read as 10 to 30 years by the generator. The shares sum to 99.9 to 100 in the source and are scaled to 10000.
sources.employment.registered_bps: IBGE, PNAD Continua quarterly, SIDRA table 4097 (people employed by position in occupation), Minas Gerais, 2nd quarter 2026 (https://apisidra.ibge.gov.br/values/t/4097/n3/31/v/4090/p/202602/c11913/all; opened and read by a research agent for this work, 2026-10-09): of 5,616 thousand private-sector employees (domestic workers apart), 1,445 thousand have no signed work card (sem carteira), 25.7%; so 74.3% are registered. HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/firms.md, "Jobs an employer does not register"): each employer of a kind registers this share of its own jobs; a job outside it is paid whole, nothing is withheld and no report names the worker. The same share is given for shops, factories and construction because the source divides employees by status, not by kind of employer (its rates by activity count own-account workers too, and are not used). sources.audit.bodies: [PLACEHOLDER] Periods: decisions every 90 days (a quarter) and accounts every 180 days (an interim, half-yearly examination between the annual audits, so that a year of the run holds two), in line with annual financial audit under INTOSAI ISSAI 1000/2000 and an audit sample of 15% of the period, at least 6 and at most 25 decisions, a size chosen for a town of 1,000 to 100,000 under ISA 530 audit sampling (not opened; to confirm). sources.public_service.appointed_by: [PLACEHOLDER] Who fills the post of a public body when none of its own staff is left: the town's council, which seconds one of its own staff to it, as a local government assigns officers to bodies it runs. Bodies run on their own account (the bank, the union, the paper, landlords, shops) are not covered: their owners or members would appoint, and no owner's or member's office exists to do it.

sources.nature.species: Callithrix penicillata (native to the Cerrado and Atlantic Forest edge). In Cerrado habitats (cerradao and dense cerrado) of the Brazilian Central Plateau: groups of 4 to 11, home range 8.25 to 18.5 ha, density 0.4 to 0.82 individuals a hectare, higher in gallery forest (Miranda and Faria 2001, Brazilian Journal of Biology / Brazilian Journal of Biology 61; found via search, paper not opened; to confirm). Density 0.8 in woodland and riverbank and 0.4 in scrub; growth, mortality and dispersal are placeholders. | Myrmecophaga tridactyla, Vulnerable (IUCN Red List; ICMBio Livro Vermelho 2018; to confirm). Density about 0.2 to 0.4 animals per square kilometre in Cerrado (0.002 to 0.004 per hectare) and a home range of the order of 300 ha (Medri and Mourao 2005 and Cerrado studies; from memory; to confirm). Growth, mortality and dispersal are placeholders (one pup a year; road-kill is a leading cause of death). | Turdus rufiventris (sabia-laranjeira), the national bird of Brazil, common and conspicuous in towns and woodland. Density and home range are placeholders (no source retrieved; a typical passerine territory is about 1 ha). | Caiman latirostris, found in wetlands and rivers of the Atlantic Forest and Cerrado; in Rio Doce State Park, Minas Gerais, an encounter rate of 4.01 individuals a kilometre of water body was recorded (found via search from Brazilian herpetological literature, paper not opened; to confirm). Converted by the cell size to about 1.6 an hectare of riverbank cell (an estimate); the wetland density, home range, growth and mortality are placeholders. IUCN Least Concern (to confirm). Tolerance of pollution is a placeholder.
